title: 3rd Truth The Importance Of This Mystery And Reference To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What central issue does this passage say is being explained and proven in this section?
questions.answer: It is explaining the mystery of Divine oneness shown in the fact that creating the greatest thing and the smallest thing is equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why is this issue described as especially important for Islam and faith?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a major foundation for belief, a deep source of iman, and a key to understanding creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation of the mystery makes possible for a person to understand?
questions.answer: It makes possible an understanding of the hidden secret of how all beings are created.

questions.question: How is philosophy portrayed in relation to this mystery?
questions.answer: Philosophy is described as unable to solve it and left powerless before it.

questions.question: What role is attributed to the Risale-i Nur in this discussion?
questions.answer: It is said to have solved, clarified, and firmly demonstrated this mystery.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say those proofs are?
questions.answer: It says they are established with the same certainty as a basic mathematical fact.

questions.question: Why does the passage not give a full treatment of the issue here?
questions.answer: Because the fuller explanation is assigned to other parts of the Risale-i Nur, and only a brief outline is intended here.

questions.question: How many mysteries does the speaker plan to mention, and what are they compared to?
questions.answer: Thirteen are mentioned, and they are compared to steps or a table of contents.

questions.question: Why was the full set not completed?
questions.answer: Two strong obstacles, one physical and one non-physical, prevented the rest from being written.

questions.question: What “mystery” is the passage mainly concerned with in this section?
questions.answer: It is concerned with how Allah creates very large and very small things with no difference in difficulty.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the value of understanding this mystery?
questions.answer: It describes it as highly beneficial, deeply meaningful, and central to religious belief.

questions.question: What does this explanation do in relation to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It is said to unlock one of the Qur’an’s deep meanings.

questions.question: What effect does this have on human attempts to explain creation without revelation?
questions.answer: It shows that human philosophy cannot fully handle this issue.

questions.question: What attitude of gratitude appears in the passage toward Allah?
questions.answer: Strong praise and repeated thanks are offered for allowing this mystery to be clarified.

questions.question: Which work is credited with demonstrating this matter?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is credited with demonstrating it.

questions.question: Does the passage aim to repeat all the detailed proofs here or to summarize them? Explain.
questions.answer: It aims to summarize them briefly and point to their foundations, not restate all the full arguments.

questions.question: What happened after the first two mysteries were written?
questions.answer: The rest were left unfinished because of two serious obstacles.

questions.question: What principle begins the First Mystery?
questions.answer: If something belongs essentially to a thing, its opposite cannot enter that essence.

questions.question: What examples are used to explain how degrees arise in ordinary things?
questions.answer: Light and darkness, heat and cold, and strength and resistance.

questions.question: Why are there no higher and lower levels in Divine power?
questions.answer: Because no opposite mixes into it, so it remains perfect and undivided.

questions.question: What practical consequence follows from Divine power having no degrees?
questions.answer: No obstacle can resist it, and no created thing is harder to make than another.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the creation of a flower, a tree, spring, and resurrection?
questions.answer: It presents them as all equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What argument is made about the denial of Divine unity?
questions.answer: Without Divine unity, creating small things would become just as hard as creating large things, or even harder.

questions.question: How does this support belief in Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: The ease, order, and artistic beauty seen in abundant creation point to one all-powerful Creator.

questions.question: In the Second Mystery, why is the image of sunlight in many mirrors important?
questions.answer: It helps explain how one source can produce many reflections at the same time.

questions.question: According to the opening paragraph, what truth about Divine unity is being uncovered?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah’s creating of universals and particulars is equal in ease.

questions.question: Why does the passage present this truth as more than just an abstract idea?
questions.answer: Because it says this truth is a core support for Islam, faith, and understanding the world.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest happens when this truth is understood?
questions.answer: A person gains access to a hidden meaning behind the existence and creation of beings.

questions.question: What is implied by saying that philosophy is left helpless before this issue?
questions.answer: It implies that reason by itself cannot fully solve this deepest problem of creation.

questions.question: What tone does the passage use when speaking about the Risale-i Nur’s contribution?
questions.answer: It uses a grateful and praising tone.

questions.question: How does the passage support its high view of the Risale-i Nur’s proof?
questions.answer: By saying its arguments are decisive and as certain as an obvious mathematical truth.

questions.question: Why are only the foundations of the argument given here?
questions.answer: Because the full demonstrations are located elsewhere, so this section only introduces the main steps.

questions.question: What do the thirteen mysteries function like in the structure of the discussion?
questions.answer: They function like stages in an argument or headings in an outline.

questions.question: What prevented the treatment from continuing beyond the second mystery?
questions.answer: Two major barriers, one outward and one inward, stopped it.

questions.question: In the First Mystery, what is the relationship between Divine power and the Divine Essence?
questions.answer: Divine power is inseparable from Allah’s Essence.

questions.question: What does that relationship rule out?
questions.answer: It rules out any possibility of weakness entering Divine power.

questions.question: How does the passage explain variation in created qualities such as strength or heat?
questions.answer: It explains variation by the presence of opposing influences.

questions.question: What inference does the passage make from the absence of any opposite in Divine power?
questions.answer: Divine power has no stages, no weakness, and no limitation.

questions.question: How does this inference answer the question of whether any act is hard for Allah?
questions.answer: It answers that no act is hard for Him at all.

questions.question: What repeated pattern in the examples of resurrection, spring, tree, and flower is meant to teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that scale does not matter to Divine power.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast Divine unity with its denial in terms of creation?
questions.answer: With Divine unity, creation is easy and beautiful; without it, even simple creation becomes overwhelmingly difficult.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention abundance together with value and artistry?
questions.answer: To show that many things can be produced quickly without losing precision, worth, or beauty.

questions.question: What happens to living things after they carry out their roles, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They pass on, leaving their seeds behind in their place.

questions.question: What main claim about creation is at the heart of this target passage?
questions.answer: The main claim is that Allah creates everything, whether immense or tiny, with the same ease.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this claim as a key to understanding tawhid?
questions.answer: Because it shows that unlimited Divine power works equally across all levels of creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say this understanding reveals about the universe?
questions.answer: It reveals a hidden secret behind how all beings come into existence.

questions.question: How is non-revealed philosophy evaluated in this section?
questions.answer: It is shown as unable to unlock this deepest secret.

questions.question: What response does the speaker have after mentioning that this mystery has been solved?
questions.answer: The speaker responds with intense gratitude and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What source is said to provide the proof for this mystery?
questions.answer: The proof is said to be found in the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Why does the passage point readers to other sections instead of developing every proof here?
questions.answer: Because those sections already explain the matter in detail, while this part is only a brief introduction.

questions.question: What was the intended scope of the discussion after this introduction?
questions.answer: It was meant to continue through thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What interrupted that plan?
questions.answer: Two serious obstacles, one material and one immaterial.

questions.question: What logical rule is introduced at the beginning of the First Mystery?
questions.answer: An essential attribute cannot admit its opposite into the same essence.

questions.question: How is that rule applied to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Since power belongs essentially to Allah, powerlessness cannot enter His Essence.

questions.question: What examples are used to show how degrees appear in created things?
questions.answer: The passage gives examples from light, temperature, and physical force.

questions.question: Why does Divine power not increase or decrease?
questions.answer: Because nothing contrary to it mixes with it, so it has no gradation.

questions.question: What follows from the fact that Divine power has no gradation?
questions.answer: Nothing can hinder it, and no task is more difficult than another.

questions.question: How does the passage use the examples of flower, tree, spring, and resurrection?
questions.answer: It uses them to show that acts that look unequal to us are equal before Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage say would happen if there were no Divine unity?
questions.answer: Creation would become hard, slow, and lacking in the artistic perfection we now see.

questions.question: What evidence from the natural world is used to support the claim of Divine ease?
questions.answer: The regular appearance of abundant, beautiful, and purposeful living things is used as evidence.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of one sun appearing in many mirrors?
questions.answer: One source can give to countless recipients at once without being divided or burdened.

questions.question: What is the “word of unity” being clarified in this section?
questions.answer: It is the truth that Allah’s oneness is seen in the equal ease of creating the largest and smallest things.

questions.question: Why is this called a “mystery” in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is a deep truth that is not obvious to ordinary reasoning and needs to be unveiled.

questions.question: What religious importance is attached to this truth?
questions.answer: It is treated as one of the strongest supports of Islam and faith.

questions.question: What intellectual benefit comes from understanding it?
questions.answer: It helps a person grasp a hidden secret of existence that ordinary philosophy cannot solve.

questions.question: What work is praised for explaining this matter?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is praised for explaining it.

questions.question: How firm does the passage claim its arguments are?
questions.answer: It claims they are fully convincing and as clear as a simple arithmetic certainty.

questions.question: Why are readers referred elsewhere for the full explanation?
questions.answer: Because this section chooses to present only the basis and a short outline.

questions.question: What stopped the author from completing the rest?
questions.answer: Both outward and inward obstacles stopped the work.

questions.question: What impossible thing would happen if an essence admitted its opposite, according to the First Mystery?
questions.answer: Contradictory realities would unite in one essence, which is impossible.

questions.question: How does that principle defend the perfection of Divine power?
questions.answer: It shows that weakness can never touch Divine power because power belongs essentially to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the existence of stronger and weaker forms in created things?
questions.answer: Such differences come from interference by opposites.

questions.question: Why can no such stronger-weaker scale exist in Divine power?
questions.answer: Because no opposite can enter it at all.

questions.question: What does this teach about difficulties in creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that what seems hard or easy to us makes no difference to Allah.

questions.question: Which examples are used to make that point vivid?
questions.answer: The passage compares resurrection with spring, spring with a tree, and a tree with a flower.

questions.question: What negative consequence follows from rejecting Divine unity?
questions.answer: Even ordinary creation would become extremely difficult and lose its excellence.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the created things we constantly see around us?
questions.answer: It describes them as plentiful, valuable, skillfully made, and produced swiftly and regularly.

questions.question: In the Second Mystery, what does luminosity help explain?
questions.answer: It helps explain how one source can be manifested in many places at the same time.

questions.question: What major theological problem is this passage trying to solve?
questions.answer: It is trying to explain how Allah’s unity is shown by His equal ease in creating all things, no matter their size or number.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect this issue so strongly to faith?
questions.answer: Because understanding it strengthens belief in Allah’s power, oneness, and lordship over creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say becomes known when this mystery is opened?
questions.answer: The hidden secret behind the creation of all beings becomes known.

questions.question: What limit does the passage place on philosophy?
questions.answer: It says philosophy cannot successfully overcome this problem on its own.

questions.question: How does the passage express appreciation for the explanation of this matter?
questions.answer: It offers abundant praise and thanks to Allah for allowing it to be made clear.

questions.question: What text is said to have given decisive proof for this explanation?
questions.answer: The decisive proof is said to be in the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this section if the detailed proofs are elsewhere?
questions.answer: Its purpose is to lay out the foundations briefly and point toward the larger explanation.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of only the first and second mysteries being written?
questions.answer: The discussion was intended to continue much further but remained incomplete.

questions.question: What two kinds of barriers caused that incompletion?
questions.answer: One was material and the other was immaterial.

questions.question: In simple terms, what is the core idea of the First Mystery?
questions.answer: What truly belongs to Allah’s Essence cannot be invaded by its opposite.

questions.question: What opposite of power is specifically denied of Allah?
questions.answer: Powerlessness or incapacity is denied of Him.

questions.question: How are degrees in ordinary created qualities explained?
questions.answer: They arise when something contrary enters and limits the quality.

questions.question: What does the absence of such limitation mean for Divine power?
questions.answer: It means Divine power is perfect, undivided, and without levels of more or less.

questions.question: How does the passage connect that perfection to creation?
questions.answer: It says no obstacle can resist Divine power and no created thing is difficult for it.

questions.question: What do the examples of flower, tree, spring, and resurrection reveal about human assumptions?
questions.answer: They overturn the human assumption that larger acts must be harder for Allah than smaller ones.

questions.question: What does the passage say creation would be like without Divine unity?
questions.answer: It would be strained, delayed, and stripped of much of its order and artistry.

questions.question: How do seeds fit into the argument about living things?
questions.answer: They show that creatures depart after fulfilling their duties but leave continuity behind in an ordered way.

questions.question: What shared lesson comes from the examples of mirrors, ears, and luminous beings?
questions.answer: One source can act in many places at once without confusion or hardship.
